newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Mosque named after top communist in Kazakhstan.
newsitem.headline: Mosque named after top communist in Kazakhstan.

text.p: Kazakh town have named their city's first mosque after a one-time communist official in the former Soviet republic, the official KazTAG news agency said on Thursday.
The agency said the mosque in the town of Leninigorsk,
named after Soviet state founder Vladimir Lenin, had been named after Soviet-era leader Dinmukhamed Kunayev.
"To give mosques the names even of well-known people is
not a Muslim tradition," it added.
Citizens of Kazakhstan have mixed feelings about
Kunayev's epoch which lasted for about three decades.
Some dislike him for his communist views, while others
say he did a lot for Kazakhstan, thanks to his cordial relations with then Soviet leader Leonid Brezhnev.
Kunayev was dismissed by Mikhail Gorbachev in 1986 and replaced with an ethnic Russian, a decision which prompted riots in the capital Almaty.
He died in 1993 at the age of 81. A central streets and a college in Almaty already bear his name.
